Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's Q3 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; David Kim, Chief Investment Officer; and Jennifer Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2023. We delivered strong results, driven by improved loss ratio trends through better claims frequency and severity management, a solid combined ratio across segments reflecting underwriting discipline, meaningful reinsurance recoveries bolstering our reserves, declining customer acquisition costs enhancing efficiency, and robust realized and unrealized gains alongside optimized asset allocation in our investment portfolio. We are particularly excited about the initial success of our ZenithNext platform and its positive impact on claims processing and risk selection.

Michael Chen, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included favorable underwriting results, higher investment income, reinsurance support, and cost efficiencies. Our combined ratio was 93.4%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.2 billion, reflecting strong performance in our fixed income segment. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with a risk-based capital ratio of 450%.

Turning now to our underwriting performance, with a particular focus on loss ratio trends and their key drivers—claims frequency and severity—across our property and casualty segments. Our combined ratio remains a cornerstone of our disciplined underwriting culture here at Zenith Insurance Group, and I'm pleased to report that for Q3 2023, our overall P&C loss ratio came in at 91.8%, a 140-basis-point improvement from 93.2% in the prior-year quarter, and down 80 basis points sequentially from Q2. On a calendar-year-to-date basis through September, we're at 92.4%, positioning us well toward our full-year guidance of 91-93%.

This favorable trend reflects the results of our multi-year initiatives in pricing adequacy, risk selection, and advanced analytics, even as we navigated persistent inflationary pressures and elevated catastrophe activity. Frequency, which we measure as claims per earned policy exposure or per $100 of earned premium in some lines, moderated across most books in Q3. Overall P&C frequency was down 3% year-over-year, driven by personal auto where frequency declined 4.5% YoY, with bodily injury claims per 100 cars falling to 2.8 from 3.1. This continues a multi-quarter downtrend, attributable to our expanded telematics adoption—now penetrating 28% of our policies via our ZenithDrive app, which uses machine learning to score driving behavior and adjust premiums in real-time. Our integration with Apple CarPlay has accelerated uptake. Homeowners frequency was flat to down 1% YoY, despite a mild uptick in water damage claims from aging infrastructure in the Midwest. Commercial multi-peril was down 6% YoY, reflecting improved workplace safety protocols post-COVID and our selective underwriting in small business segments.

However, liability lines saw a modest 2% frequency uptick due to social inflation—litigation trends akin to those pressuring peers like Travelers and Chubb. Severity remains the primary headwind, up 7% YoY on an index basis adjusted for mix, pushing average claim costs higher amid broad-based inflation. Auto physical damage severity rose 11% YoY to $4,200 per claim, fueled by a 15% surge in repair labor rates now averaging $55/hour nationally and OEM parts pricing, exacerbated by supply chain bottlenecks lingering from the 2022 chip shortage. Used vehicle values are still 20% above pre-pandemic levels per Manheim indices. Property catastrophe ex-cat severity was up 8% due to reconstruction cost inflation—labor up 12%, materials like lumber and roofing up 9%. We absorbed $450 million in pre-tax cat losses in Q3, primarily from California wildfires impacting our high-value coastal book and Southeast hurricanes, representing 65% of our $692 million total cat hit YTD. This compares to industry benchmarks from ISO Verisk, where large losses averaged $15 million per event. Workers' comp and general liability severity climbed 9% YoY, driven by medical cost trends up 6% per our actuarial models and opioid/alternative therapy litigation, mirroring Travelers' recent disclosures.

Net of these drivers, our underlying loss ratio—stripping out cats and prior-year development—was 88.5% in Q3, a 200 bps improvement YoY, underscoring rate and exposure management efficacy. Regionally, U.S. at 82% of P&C premiums had a loss ratio of 92.5%, benefiting from 9.2% average earned rate increases over the past two renewals. Southeast frequency pressured by storm activity, but West Coast severity mitigated by our 15% reduction in high-risk wildfire exposure via stricter mitigation credits like requiring Class 4 impact-resistant roofs. Europe at 10% of premiums was strong at 89.2%, aided by benign weather and our partnership with AXA on flood reinsurance towers. UK motor severity eased post-Brexit supply normalization. Asia-Pacific at 5% of premiums was 95.1%, reflecting Thailand floods with $120 million impact and Japan earthquake risks, but offset by 12% rate hikes in commercial lines. Other international at 3% was elevated at 97%, due to Latin American inflation volatility; we're actively non-renewing underperforming accounts.

Our loss ratio compression stems from targeted actions: our new GenAI platform, rolled out in Q2 with IBM Watson integration, has reduced cycle times by 25% and straight-through processing to 45% for auto glass claims, curbing severity leakage from prolonged handling. Generalized Linear Models refreshed with 2023 telematics and catastrophe data have enabled 5-7% embedded rate actions in renewal pricing, with elasticity testing showing minimal take-up erosion. Post the January 1 renewal, our $2 billion excess-of-loss tower—placed with leaders like Swiss Re and Munich Re—caps net cat retention at 2.5% of surplus, providing $300 million in savings YTD versus expiring terms. We've grown high-margin segments like cyber with loss ratio 82% and small commercial package at 87%, while trimming E&S liability exposure by 8%.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 loss ratio in the low 92s, with full-year ex-cat at 89-90%. Risks include further social inflation—we're stress-testing for 5% annual increases—and potential La Niña-driven cats, but our $1.2 billion in pricing tailwinds and 20% telematics penetration target by YE24 position us for sub-90% underlying ratios in 2024—competitive with Berkshire Hathaway P&C's trajectory.

Now, focusing on our combined ratio, both overall and by segment, which remains a cornerstone of our profitability in this dynamic P&C landscape. The combined ratio is our incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses plus other underwriting expenses, divided by earned premiums. A ratio below 100% signals underwriting profit, and we've consistently delivered here through disciplined pricing, superior risk selection, and operational excellence.

Our overall accident-year combined ratio for Q3 came in at 93.4%, a 270 basis point improvement from 96.1% in Q3 2022, and 110 basis points better than our Q2 2023 result of 94.5%. This marks our best quarterly performance since Q1 2020, pre-pandemic. Excluding catastrophe losses—which totaled $285 million this quarter, or 4.2 points on the ratio, driven by California wildfires and Southeast hurricanes—we achieved 89.2% combined ratio, underscoring the underlying health of our book.

Breaking it down: our loss ratio was 65.2%, up 240 basis points year-over-year due to elevated severity from social inflation and repair costs amid persistent supply chain disruptions. However, this was partially offset by 1.8 points of favorable prior year development, primarily in our commercial auto and workers' comp lines where reserve redundancies emerged from better-than-expected claim closures. Our expense ratio improved to 28.2%, down 110 basis points from last year, reflecting commission reductions from higher retained premiums and efficiencies from our AI-powered claims platform, which processed 42% of claims digitally this quarter—up from 28% a year ago.

By segment, across our three core P&C segments: Personal Lines at 55% of earned premiums had a combined ratio of 91.5%, 320 basis points better than Q3 2022's 94.7%. Earned premiums grew 12% to $2.8 billion, fueled by 8% rate adequacy gains and 5% policy count growth from our direct-to-consumer digital channels. Personal auto, 70% of segment, was 89.2% combined ratio—elite territory, rivaling peers like Progressive. Loss ratio held at 61.5%, benefiting from our ZenithDrive telematics program, now with 3.2 million enrolled policyholders, delivering 15% lower loss rates for safe drivers. Frequency ticked up 2% from litigated rear-enders in urban markets like Miami and Atlanta, but severity moderated via vendor partnerships with Solera for streamlined repair estimating. Expense ratio: 27.8%, aided by 20% reduction in agent commissions through app-based quoting. Homeowners & Other, 30%, was 98.7%, pressured by 7.2 points of cat losses from California wildfires and Hurricane Idalia. Ex-cats, it's 91.5%, with earned premiums up 14% from mid-teen rate hikes in high-risk coastal states. We've proactively non-renewed 45,000 policies in wildfire-prone ZIP codes, partnering with GeoVerra for advanced cat modeling that shaved 1.1 points off our modeled loss estimates.

Commercial Lines: 94.3%, improved 450 basis points year-over-year from 98.8%, with earned premiums expanding 9% to $1.5 billion. This segment faced headwinds from workers' comp severity—up 5% due to OSHA-mandated wage escalations—but our pure premium focus and mid-market sweet spot kept us resilient. Loss ratio at 67.1%, including 2.4 points unfavorable development in general liability from social inflation trends seen industry-wide. We countered with 6% net rate increases and stricter underwriting guidelines via our EagleEye AI risk scorer, which flags high-litigation risks 25% more accurately. Expense ratio dipped to 27.2%, thanks to payroll leverage and our shift to 60% straight-through processing for small commercial claims. Middle-market property book delivered sub-90 ex-cat, bolstered by parametric triggers that accelerated payouts post-Hurricane Idalia, enhancing customer retention to 92%.

Specialty & Reinsurance: 87.1%, up 610 basis points from last year's 93.2%, on flat earned premiums of $750 million. This includes our E&S franchise, directors & officers, and quota share reinsurance placements. Loss ratio: 58.9%, pristine, with minimal cats at 0.8 points and 2.1 points favorable development in cyber, where silent cyber exclusions—aligned with industry leaders like Chubb—prevented bleed from supply chain hacks. D&O shone at 82% combined, capitalizing on M&A rebound; we wrote $120 million in new premium at mid-teens ROE targets. Our 30% quota share with Swiss Re on U.S. casualty risks capped volatility, while our in-house Bermuda cat reinsurer absorbed $50 million in losses at a 75% cession rate.

Regionally, U.S. at 82% of premiums was 92.1%, despite $210 million in cats—Hurricane Idalia hit our Florida homeowners hard at 9 points, but rate filings averaging 11% in Gulf states mitigated impact. California remains challenged at 102% due to wildfire mandates, prompting our 15% portfolio shrinkage there. Europe at 12% was 96.8%, hammered by Storm Babet floods at 3.5 points and softening commercial rates; we've pulled back 8% in UK motor to preserve discipline. Asia-Pacific at 6% delivered 88.5%, with strong Japan earthquake protection and growth in Australia cyber via partnerships like those with Munich Re.

Technical initiatives driving these outcomes include our $150 million ZenithNext platform rollout: machine learning for claims triage cut LAE by 12%, and usage-based insurance penetration hit 35% in personal lines, with blockchain-verified mileage for fraud prevention. On the cat front, RMS v18 models integrated with climate analytics reduced our probable maximum loss by 8% on coastal exposures.

Strategically, we're focused on accident-year ex-cat combined ratios trending toward the low-90s by year-end, targeting 91-93% for FY2023 versus guidance of 93-95%. We've actioned 7-10% rate increases across the board, with commercial renewals at 9% net, and expect $400 million in premium growth for Q4 from bundled offerings like auto-home-cyber packages. Reinsurance renewals at 1/1/24 locked in stable terms—our cat tower at $1.2 billion limit, 55% ceded—positioning us for a volatile 2024 cat season amid La Niña forecasts.

Our 93.4% overall combined ratio reflects not just tactical wins, but a fortified franchise ready for macro headwinds like inflation now cooling to 3.2% core and regulatory scrutiny on AI underwriting.

Next, on reinsurance recoveries received and expected, which played a pivotal role in our strong loss reserve development this quarter and continue to underpin our favorable net loss outlook. In Q3 2023, we recognized $1.2 billion in reinsurance recoveries received, marking a 45% increase from the $825 million recorded in Q3 2022. This uplift was driven primarily by the accelerated settlement of catastrophe claims from last year's U.S. hurricane season—Hurricane Ian and Fiona—and ongoing wildfire recoveries from California's 2022 events. Year-to-date through Q3, total recoveries received stand at $3.4 billion, up 32% from the prior-year period, representing approximately 28% of our gross incurred losses for the nine months.

Our Property & Casualty segment accounted for 85% or $1.02 billion of Q3 recoveries. Within P&C, nat cat perils dominated: $650 million from our excess-of-loss catastrophe towers, with average attachment points performing as modeled at 5% of gross ultimate loss. Our quota share treaties on non-cat property risks contributed another $250 million, benefiting from favorable commutation settlements with panels including Swiss Re and Munich Re. In Life & Health, recoveries totaled $180 million, largely from longevity and mortality experience in our U.S. group life portfolio, where we've ceded 40% via yearly renewable term arrangements with reinsurers like RGA and Hannover Re.

Regionally, the U.S. drove 62% of Q3 recoveries at $744 million, reflecting the maturation of our $15 billion catastrophe program renewed at 1 January 2023. This program features layered XoL coverage up to $10 billion per occurrence/annual aggregate, with key terms including 2.5% ceding commission and full collateralization via letters of credit from A-rated panels. Europe contributed 22% or $264 million, boosted by flood recoveries in Germany and the UK from 2021 events, where our proportional facultative placements with SCOR and PartnerRe yielded better-than-expected loss creep adjustments. Asia-Pacific added 12% or $144 million, primarily from typhoon claims in Japan and Australia, supported by our regional excess-of-loss treaties with Evergreen Re and CCR Re.

Our recovery rates remain robust at 92% of ceded paid losses YTD, a 300 basis point improvement over 2022, thanks to proactive portfolio actions. We've seen meaningful favorable prior-year development of $450 million in Q3 recoveries, reducing our net loss ratio by 520 basis points to 61.2%. This compares favorably to industry peers; while Chubb reported 88% recovery rates in their Q3 call, our diversified panel—spanning 15 reinsurers with no single exposure exceeding 15%—has insulated us from the selective underwriting hardening we've observed in the retro market.

Looking ahead to expected recoveries, we project $2.8 billion over the next 12 months as of 30 September 2023. This includes $1.6 billion in receivables already billed and collectible within 90 days, $900 million in IBNR recoverables from open cat years, and $300 million from anticipated development on attritional losses. Key assumptions here incorporate third-party actuarial reviews by firms like Milliman and Guy Carpenter, pricing in a 105% loss development factor on 2022-2023 events. We've stress-tested this at a 1-in-200 year nat cat scenario, where recoveries would cover 95% of gross losses above our retention.

Strategically, we're enhancing our reinsurance optimization through our Zenith ReTech platform, a proprietary AI-driven tool launched in H1, which has improved recovery billing accuracy by 18% via real-time matching of gross claims data against treaty wordings—reducing disputes and accelerating cash flows. At the upcoming 1 January 2024 renewals, we're targeting a 10-15% reduction in ceding commissions through performance-based incentives, while exploring innovative structures like catastrophe swaps with CCR IFC and sidecar investments totaling $500 million in capacity from investors like Stone Ridge and Fermat Capital. This builds on our 2023 renewal success, where we secured flat pricing despite 20% industry rate hikes on U.S. Gulf Coast business.

Regionally, we're leaning into growth in resilient markets: expanding Australian bushfire coverage with higher attachments via proportional treaties, and bolstering European flood programs post-DWD events through multi-year deals with Berkshire Hathaway. In the U.S., amid rising secondary peril frequency—California wildfires and Texas winter storms—we're dynamically adjusting retentions via index-triggered reinstatement premiums, preserving capital for organic growth.

Overall, these recoveries not only bolstered our Q3 adjusted operating income by $850 million but also reinforce our full-year combined ratio guidance of 92-95%. We're well-positioned to deliver mid-teens ROE in 2024, with reinsurance as a core lever for earnings stability and growth.

I'd also like to dive into our customer acquisition cost trends, which remain a cornerstone of our profitability flywheel. CAC is defined as the total marketing, sales, and distribution expenses divided by the number of new policies written in a given period. It's critically linked to our lifetime value metrics—targeting a healthy LTV-to-CAC ratio of at least 4:1 across our book—and directly impacts our combined ratio and return on equity.

In Q3 2023, our blended CAC came in at $218 per new policy, a robust 12% year-over-year decline from $248 in Q3 2022, and sequentially down 4% from Q2 this year. This marks our eighth straight quarter of CAC deflation, bringing our trailing 12-month average to $232—well below the industry benchmark of $265 as reported by SNL Financial for large P&C carriers. Excluding our legacy agent channel, which still represents 28% of new business but is shrinking, our digital-first CAC is running at just $162, underscoring the power of our omnichannel pivot.

By acquisition channel, our direct-to-consumer digital efforts—powered by our proprietary ZenithDirect app and website—delivered 62% of new policies this quarter at a CAC of $145, down 18% YoY. This is driven by a 25% uplift in organic traffic from SEO optimizations around high-intent searches like "best auto insurance rates" and "homeowners insurance quotes," alongside a 15% improvement in conversion rates from AI-driven dynamic pricing engines. Paid digital, including Google Ads and Meta platforms, saw CPA rise modestly to $89 per lead due to ongoing ad auction inflation—echoing what we've seen industry-wide post-iOS 14.5 privacy changes—but our machine learning bid management kept ROAS above 5:1.

Comparatively, our broker and agent partnerships, including embedded insurance deals with fintechs like Affirm and Klarna for point-of-sale auto and renters coverage, clocked in at $312 CAC. While higher, this channel boasts a 30% higher policy persistency rate, boosting LTV by 22% to over $1,800 per policy. We've clawed back 10% YoY here through performance-based commissions tied to loss ratios.

Regionally, the U.S.—our largest market at 65% of premiums—led with a CAC of $195, down 14% YoY, fueled by telematics adoption in personal auto lines. Our ZenithDrive program, now with 1.2 million enrolled drivers, uses usage-based insurance data to hyper-target safe-driver prospects via programmatic ads, slashing acquisition costs by 28% in that segment versus traditional quoting. In contrast, Europe, at 22% of premiums, faced headwinds with CAC at $285, up 3% YoY due to stringent GDPR compliance costs and softer demand amid elevated reinsurance pricing post-2023's Storm Ciarán. However, our Berlin-based insurtech hub has piloted usage-based home insurance with IoT partners like Bosch, piloting a 20% CAC reduction in Germany and the UK.

Asia-Pacific, our fastest-growing region at 13% of new business, hit $240 CAC, flat YoY but with a 35% volume surge from partnerships like our embedded travel insurance with Grab in Southeast Asia. Here, regulatory tailwinds in India—following IRDAI's sandbox approvals for digital-first models—have enabled us to bypass traditional bancassurance, mirroring Lemonade's playbook but at scale.

Strategically, these trends reflect our $150 million GenAI investment in 2023 paying off: Our conversational AI quoting bot, integrated with WhatsApp and SMS in emerging markets, has boosted lead-to-policy conversions by 22%, directly compressing CAC. We're accelerating embedded insurance, targeting 25% of new auto and SMB policies by year-end through APIs with e-commerce giants like Shopify—similar to Allstate's Square integration—projecting another 15-20% CAC efficiency. We're optimizing our marketing mix with a zero-based budgeting approach, reallocating 40% of spend from TV and print to addressable TV and connected TV platforms like Roku, where CPMs are 30% lower and attribution is cleaner via probabilistic matching.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 blended CAC to dip to $210-$215, assuming stable ad pricing and no major attribution disruptions from Chrome's pending cookie phase-out. This positions us to lap our 2023 growth while maintaining mid-teens premium expansion, all while keeping our expense ratio under 28%. Our LTV:CAC ratio now sits at 4.6:1 group-wide, up from 3.8:1 a year ago, giving us ample runway for selective pricing discipline amid hardening rates.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal auto line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-powered claims triage and dynamic pricing models.

David Kim: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income, with net investment income of $1.2 billion in Q3, a 12% increase quarter-over-quarter, driven by higher reinvestment yields and disciplined asset-liability management. With over $165 billion in invested assets as of September 30, 2023—up 3% from year-end 2022—our portfolio continues to deliver resilient returns amid volatility.

Specifically, on realized and unrealized gains and losses on investments, which totaled a net gain of $285 million in Q3, compared to a $112 million net loss in Q3 2022 and a $45 million net gain in Q2 2023. Realized gains and losses came in at $210 million net gain in Q3, up from $85 million in Q2. These stemmed from selective sales within our portfolio, harvesting profits on positions that met our predefined thresholds under our dynamic optimization framework. Fixed income sales realized $145 million in gains from trimming holdings in investment-grade corporate bonds, particularly in financials and industrials sectors. With the Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate Bond Index up 1.8% in Q3 following the Fed's signals, we sold $2.1 billion face value of bonds yielding an average of 4.8%—positions acquired at a blended 3.2% during the 2022 rate hike cycle. This generated a 2.1% realized yield pickup, enhancing our portfolio's overall book yield to 4.6% from 4.3% at year-end.

Equity realizations added $45 million in gains, primarily U.S. large-cap names in our S&P 500-tracking sleeve. We rotated out of overvalued tech holdings and into dividend aristocrats such as Procter & Gamble and Johnson & Johnson, yielding 3.2% on average. Equities represent 12% of our portfolio, down from 14% last year, as we de-risked ahead of election cycle uncertainty. Alternatives contributed $20 million from private credit and mortgage loans. Our $18 billion alternatives bucket, 11% of assets, benefited from early exits in direct lending deals originated at L+350 bps spreads, now reinvesting at L+425 bps amid tighter bank lending post-SVB fallout.

Regionally, U.S. fixed income drove 70% of realizations, with Europe contributing 20% via opportunistic sales in UK gilts as yields compressed 15 bps on ECB dovishness, and Asia-Pacific at 10%, harvesting gains on JGBs amid BOJ yield curve control tweaks.

Unrealized gains and losses were a $75 million net gain in Q3 versus a $30 million loss in Q2. Unrealized marks reflect fair value changes under ASC 320 and NAIC statutory accounting, with our portfolio's effective duration at 5.8 years—extended modestly from 5.4 years via Q2 ladder extensions to better match our 6-7 year P&C liability tail. Positive contributors included $420 million in unrealized gains, led by a $310 million uplift in our $110 billion fixed income sleeve, 67% of portfolio. Municipal bonds, 15% allocation, surged 2.5% on supply-demand imbalances, while RMBS gained 1.9% amid mortgage rate stabilization around 6.8%. Equities added $80 million, with our active managers outperforming the S&P 500 by 120 bps through factor tilts toward value and low-vol strategies.

Offsetting losses were $345 million in net unrealized losses, primarily from high-quality municipals and corporates still underwater from 2022's rate shock—though OTTI impairments remain negligible at under 0.1% of assets, thanks to our conservative SVO ratings with 95% NAIC 1-2. Our credit quality is pristine: 88% AAA/AA, average rating A+.

Year-to-date trends show unrealized gains improving 45% from Q4 2022 lows, as the 10-year Treasury yield fell 25 bps to 4.25%, validating our barbell strategy—short-duration TIPS at the front end yielding 2.1% real and long-duration corporates at the back.

Our investment strategy focuses on income generation for statutory surplus growth, ALM precision to support reserving for catastrophes like recent hurricanes, and prudent growth in yield-enhancing sleeves. We've deployed AI-driven portfolio optimization via our partnership with BlackRock's Aladdin platform, enabling real-time scenario testing for 50,000+ scenarios—including +200 bps rate shocks and 20% equity drawdowns. This underpinned a 15 bps compression in our risk-adjusted spread to 85 bps. Our ESG overlay now covers 40% of assets, targeting SFDR Article 8 funds with 20 bps yield premium, outperforming vanilla benchmarks by 30 bps YTD.

Regionally, U.S. at 75% of portfolio remains core, with reinvestments at 5.1% yields vs. 3.9% maturities. Europe at 15% faces headwinds from German bund volatility but benefits from 4.9% Euro IG yields. Asia at 10% is growing via RMB-denominated infrastructure debt at 5.5%, hedging currency risk with FX forwards.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 net investment gains of $250-300 million, assuming Fed funds at 5.25-5.50% and S&P volatility under 15 VIX. We're guiding to a full-year portfolio yield of 4.7-4.9%, with alternatives scaling to 13% by year-end through opportunistic GP stakes.

Before we open for questions, a detailed overview of our asset allocation strategy, with $258 billion in invested assets as of September 30—up 4% year-over-year. Our portfolio is designed to support our $185 billion in insurance liabilities while delivering superior risk-adjusted returns. Our book yield stood at 4.2% for the quarter, a 15 basis point improvement from Q2, driven by tactical repositioning amid the Fed's rate hiking cycle.

Fixed income: 74% of the portfolio at $191 billion, anchoring stability for liability matching in our life, P&C, and annuity lines. Average portfolio duration of 6.2 years—slightly extended from 5.9 years last quarter—to capture higher yields in the inverted yield curve, within ALM guidelines. Credit quality investment-grade dominant, 88% rated A or better per S&P, NAIC 1-2 at 92%. Breakdown: U.S. Treasuries and agency MBS at 32% of total fixed income ($61 billion), yielding 4.8% with minimal spread compression; investment-grade corporates at 45% ($86 billion), overweighted financials and utilities like JPMorgan and NextEra Energy; RMBS/ABS at 15% ($29 billion), focusing on prime auto and equipment lease securitizations for 5.5% yields with low delinquency under 1.2%.

Regionally for fixed income: U.S. benefited from 10-year Treasury yields at 4.3%, boosting new money to 5.1%. Europe, 18% ($34 billion), pivoted from German Bunds to UK gilts and peripheral sovereigns amid ECB tightening, Eurozone IG corporates at 4.2%—a 50 bps pickup. Asia-Pacific, 12% ($23 billion), emphasizes JGBs and AUD corporates, hedging via FX forwards. Performance was solid at 2.8% total return, outpacing Bloomberg U.S. Aggregate by 40 bps.

Equities: 13% at $34 billion, providing growth for long-duration products, at the high end of our 10-15% band. 65% U.S. equities ($22 billion), indexed to S&P 500 with tilts to dividend aristocrats like Procter & Gamble and Johnson & Johnson (yield 3.1%); 20% international developed ($7 billion) via MSCI EAFE ETF overlays; 15% emerging markets ($5 billion) in Taiwan semis and Indian financials. Q3 delivered 5.2% returns, led by tech rebound, but derisked by 2% via covered call overlays generating $120 million in premium. Leveraging BlackRock's Aladdin for factor analysis—momentum, value, quality—at beta 0.85. Asia equities trimmed 10% favoring Vietnam and Indonesia.

Alternatives: 10% at $26 billion, targeting 6-8% IRRs. Private equity 40% ($10 billion), secondaries from KKR and Carlyle at 14% net IRR; real assets 35% ($9 billion), core real estate conversions in Sunbelt and renewables via Brookfield at 7.2%; hedge funds/credit 25% ($7 billion), event-driven from Citadel and direct lending at SOFR+450 bps. Initiated $2 billion climate-resilient infrastructure with BlackRock's decarbonization funds, aligning with NAIC climate rules. Q3 distributions $450 million. Regionally: 40% U.S., 30% Europe green bonds, 20% Asia data centers, 10% LatAm EM debt.

Cash and other: 3% ($7 billion) in T-bills and money markets at 5.2%.

Portfolio-wide, yield curve steepening benefits new money at 5.0% vs. 3.8% a year ago. ROA improved to 2.9%, supporting 12-14% RBC target. Advancing AI-driven scenario modeling for 200 bps rate shocks and drawdowns. Compared to peers, our mix positions for 4.5% book yield by year-end. Risk-wise, vigilant on CRE (3% exposure, 85% office trimmed). Expect modest alt inflows if yields stabilize above 4%, with ESG integration.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on loss ratio trends and drivers like claims frequency and severity?

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, John. As Michael detailed, our loss ratio improved to 91.8% in Q3, driven by 3% lower frequency overall, with standout declines in personal auto from telematics at 28% penetration via ZenithDrive. Severity up 7% YoY remains a challenge from inflation in repairs and cats, but our underlying ex-cat ratio at 88.5% shows the strength of our pricing and AI initiatives. We're on track for low-92s in Q4.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of elevated catastrophe activity on your business?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Emily. Cats added 4.2 points to the combined ratio this quarter, with $285 million from wildfires and hurricanes, but our reinsurance program recovered $650 million from XoL towers, capping retention effectively. We've reduced high-risk exposures like 15% in California wildfires and expect our $2.8 billion in upcoming recoveries to support stability amid La Niña risks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Lee: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes around AI underwriting on your strategy?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Robert. Regulatory scrutiny on AI is increasing, but our ZenithNext and EagleEye tools are transparent and compliant, with third-party audits. We've embedded explainability in models to meet emerging rules, and this hasn't slowed our 25% cycle time reductions or 45% straight-through processing. It positions us ahead as peers catch up.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks. On customer acquisition costs, how sustainable is the decline, and any update on embedded insurance?
